Attenuation depends on #14

  • The target that is being traversed:
  • Atomic number Z = proton nr. = electon nr.
  • Density (particle nr./volume)
  • Thickness

Notes: The relative number of photons that interact increases with the increased density, thickness, and atomic number of the object. In (A), the object in the path of the photon is thicker, denser, and composed of heavier atoms than that of the object depicted in (B); hence, the photon is much more likely to be attenuated in (A).

It has been widely adopted by hospitals. Dosimetry #32

  • Absorbed dose = the energy absorbed per unit of mass
  • - measured in Gy (1Gy = 1J/kg)
  • Equivalent dose = the absorbed dose taking the type of radiation into account (X- rays, protons, α-particles, etc.)
  • = absorbed dose x WR (WR= radiation weighting factor )
  • - measured in Sv (1Sv= 1J/kg)
  • Effective dose = the equivalent dose taking the radiation sensitivity of the tissue into account
  • = equivalent dose x WT (WT= tissue correction factor)
  • - measured in Sv (1Sv= 1J/kg)
